Task: Write spec.md (user story, goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria)
DoD: spec.md exists and clearly states the user story, what's in scope, what's out of scope, and the exact numbers that count as a successful test run.

Task: Write plan.md (architecture, data contracts, judge prompt design, decisions)
DoD: plan.md exists and every open design question has a real decision written down, not left blank.

Task: Write tasks.md
DoD: tasks.md exists and breaks every PBI into small tasks specific enough that nobody has to ask 'what do you mean' before starting one.

Task: Stakeholder review of spec/plan/tasks; refine and sign off
DoD: Someone has actually read spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md and said 'yes, build this' - silence doesn't count as approval.

Task: Initialise Python project, repo, lint config, virtualenv
DoD: Running the install command works with no errors, and the linter (ruff) reports zero problems.

Task: Configure env vars for provider API keys (.env)
DoD: .env.example lists all three required keys (OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq) with no real secrets inside it, and the real .env file is excluded from git.

Task: Define core Pydantic schemas per plan.md's data contracts
DoD: Every data shape from plan.md (EvalRun, LLMCallResult, etc.) exists as a schema, and each one can successfully load a small hand-written sample without crashing.

Task: Finalise EvalRun input JSON format + example input file
DoD: A real example JSON file exists with multiple prompt variants and test cases, and it loads successfully into the EvalRun schema with no errors.

Task: Build the template renderer
DoD: Given one prompt variant and one test case, the renderer returns the template with every {blank} correctly replaced by the real value.

Task: Unit tests: full matrix + missing-variable error case
DoD: Tests exist and pass proving every variant/test-case combo renders correctly, and that a missing variable produces a clear, readable error instead of a raw crash.

Task: Integrate litellm against OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq
DoD: One function can send a prompt to any of the three providers (OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq) just by changing the model name string.

Task: Build async parallel runner (asyncio.gather + Semaphore)
DoD: Multiple calls fire at the same time instead of one-by-one, and the number running at once never goes above the concurrency limit.

Task: Capture input/output tokens + latency per call
DoD: Every successful call's result includes the real input token count, output token count, and how many milliseconds it took.

Task: Add retry/backoff; populate error field on final failure
DoD: A temporary failure (like a rate limit) gets retried automatically with increasing wait times; if it still fails after retries, the result's error field is filled in instead of the program crashing.

Task: Write the judge prompt template
DoD: The judge prompt template exists and includes the rubric, the candidate answer, and clear instructions to return only JSON with a score and reasoning.

Task: Send judge prompt to judge model (temp 0); validate against JudgeResult
DoD: A real judge call returns a score from 1-5 plus reasoning text, and it loads correctly into the JudgeResult schema.

Task: Handle judge parse failures (retry once, fallback score=0)
DoD: If the judge's response isn't valid JSON, the program asks again once; if it still fails, the result gets a score of 0 and a 'parse failure' reason instead of crashing.

Task: Unit tests with mocked judge responses
DoD: Tests exist and pass for three cases: a valid JSON response, a broken JSON response, and a JSON response wrapped in markdown formatting.

Task: Aggregate into VariantScore + weighted_score
DoD: Each prompt variant gets one combined score built from its average quality, cost, and speed, using the weighting formula from plan.md.

Task: Recommendation generator with rationale
DoD: The program picks exactly one winning variant and writes a plain-English reason for why each other variant scored lower (quality, cost, or speed).

Task: Report formatter (CLI table + optional Markdown/JSON)
DoD: Running a report prints a readable ranked table in the terminal and also saves the full results to a JSON file.

Task: Build cli.py entry point: prompteval run <input.json> [--judge-model] [--concurrency] [--timeout] [--format]
DoD: Typing 'prompteval run <file>' in a real terminal works as an actual command, and passing --judge-model/--concurrency/--timeout/--format changes its behavior instead of being ignored.

Task: Wire pipeline: load input -> render -> execute -> judge -> score -> report
DoD: One single command runs the entire tool start to finish -- load the file, render prompts, call the AI, judge the answers, rank them, and save a report -- with no separate scripts needed.

Task: Full E2E run on one real task through all three providers
DoD: Running the tool for real - 3 prompt variants x 5 test cases against all three providers - produces a complete report with no crashes.

Task: Write README.md
DoD: README.md lets someone install the tool, set up their API keys, and run their first evaluation using only the instructions in that file.

Task: Final bug fixes/polish from E2E run
DoD: Every issue found during the real end-to-end run in T8.1 has been fixed and re-tested.

Task: Add `prompteval init` -- asks for task name, prompt variants, test cases, and rubric in the terminal, then saves a real input file
DoD: Answering the terminal questions produces a real input file that `prompteval run` can load and execute with no manual edits needed.

Task: Add `prompteval quickstart` -- AI generates a random task (or uses one you type) plus 5 test cases; user types 3 prompts; the evaluation runs immediately with no separate file/run step
DoD: Running the command with no pre-made file, answering only the task and 3 prompts, produces a real ranked report -- proven live with a genuine AI-generated task, 5 generated test cases, and a real evaluation run.

Task: Make quickstart the default when `prompteval` is run with no subcommand (or only flags)
DoD: Typing plain 'prompteval' (or 'prompteval --judge-model x') with no subcommand at all starts the quickstart flow directly; 'prompteval run <file>' and 'prompteval init' still work exactly as before.

Task: Add `prompteval /help` (also `help`/`-h`/`--help`) -- a warm, example-filled guide instead of argparse's terse default; add a clear message instead of a crash when no API key is configured at all
DoD: Typing 'prompteval /help' in a real terminal (PowerShell, confirmed) prints a full walkthrough. Running any real command with zero API keys set prints a clear fix-it message and exits cleanly instead of crashing deep inside a network call.

Task: Add `prompteval improve` -- asks for ONE prompt only (no separate context question), AI generates 3 realistic scenarios from the prompt's own wording and actually runs it against them, then returns a strict score (1-5) + reasoning + a rewritten, improved prompt (structured JSON, not prose)
DoD: Running the real command with just a prompt (no context asked) produces a real 1-5 score, reasoning grounded in real outputs, and a genuinely rewritten prompt, saved to a real markdown file -- confirmed live.

Task: Add 'Run PromtEval.cmd' -- double-click launches quickstart with no venv activation and no flags needed, stays open afterward so results are readable
DoD: Double-clicking (simulated via a real piped PowerShell invocation) launches the tool, completes a real run, and the window stays open on 'Press any key to continue' instead of vanishing.

Task: Bug fix found via the run button: a stray BOM character injected by PowerShell's stdin piping made a 'blank' wizard answer look non-empty, silently skipping AI task generation
DoD: Re-running the same real scenario after the fix shows a proper AI-generated task name instead of an empty/garbled one; added a regression test using a real BOM character so this can't silently regress.

Task: Change the no-subcommand default (bare 'prompteval' and the double-click .cmd) from quickstart to improve, since single-prompt scoring turned out to be the actually wanted default flow
DoD: Bare 'prompteval' and double-clicking 'Run PromtEval.cmd' both now go straight into the improve flow (asks for one prompt, returns score + rewrite) -- confirmed with two separate live runs. 'quickstart'/'init'/'run' still work unchanged when named explicitly.

Task: Build pricing table ($ per input/output token)
DoD: A pricing table exists listing $ per input token and $ per output token for every in-scope model.

Task: Compute cost_usd per call/variant
DoD: Given a call's real token counts, the calculated dollar cost matches what you'd get doing the multiplication by hand.

Task: Confirm partial failures never drop completed results
DoD: If some calls in a batch fail, the finished ones are still included in the final report - nothing gets thrown away.

Task: Add explicit per-provider timeout handling
DoD: A call that hangs past the timeout limit gets cancelled and recorded as a timeout error, instead of hanging forever.
